description: Fixed, skill-package-versioned. Copied verbatim into every vault by setup-slipbox — never edited per-vault, never register-matched to an individual user's corpus. This file only flags; it never auto-rewrites.
before_applying: Read style-profile.json (or stated_style.json fallback if no corpus exists) for this vault's own punctuation fingerprint, lexicon, and forbidden-vocabulary list. Signals below are generic; that file is what makes a flag specific to this user's actual voice.

mechanical.description: Signals a CLI can pattern-match automatically: literal word/phrase lists and measurable properties compared against style-profile.json baselines.
mechanical.clustering_rule: require 2+ distinct mechanical signals firing in the same passage before flagging it — a single hit is not enough
mechanical.language_gating: the mechanical word/phrase lists below are English-specific and must NOT be applied to passages outside the vault's own style-profile.json language.primary / language.additional

signals.comparison: compare against the vault's own style-profile.json baseline field, not a fixed threshold — read that field at check time

signals.note: "navigate" only counts as a metaphor for handling a topic

signals.comparison: compare against the vault's own style-profile.json baseline field, not a fixed threshold — read that field at check time

phrases: at the end of the day
it's not just about x, it's about y

notes.at the end of the day: only counts as a throwaway transition

signals.versioning: gets updated centrally as AI-vocabulary trends shift and ships with skill releases, never edited per-vault; setup-slipbox re-copies this file on every re-run, so a vault picks up package-level updates rather than staying frozen at first-setup content

judgment.description: Stays prose. Applied by whichever ground-* skill uses this file — an LLM reading the passage — because it requires reading-comprehension judgment a literal pattern-match can't do. Never mechanized.

signals.name: Negative parallelism ("not x, but y")
signals.description: The construction itself is legitimate; what's flagged is using it as a rhetorical crutch, which requires reading the actual content.

signals.name: Rule-of-three constructions used as a rhetorical crutch
signals.description: Flagged when the construction is used as a rhetorical crutch rather than because the content actually has three parts.

signals.name: Superficial "-ing" analysis clauses
signals.description: Clauses that restate the sentence's own claim instead of adding information.
